clause_only.clause: 'infra is a declaration, not a selection' — the platform-role gate on declaring a Namespace infra

matches.clause: isolated tier / no emergency break-glass path (principles 2,4,6)
matches.reason: Both argue a good-faith emergency responder is functionally blocked from needed network access with no fast lawful path, contradicting the spirit of conditional policy.

clause_only.why_not: A2 objects to punishing routine administrative labeling lag; B4 objects to blocking a live emergency incident responder — different underlying harms.

clause_only.clause: infra is a declaration, not a selection / platform-role gating (ADR-0022)

clause_only.clause: platform-role gating of infra declarations (principle 12/13, ADR-0022)
clause_only.why_not: A3 attacks the silent-render-to-isolated consequence for a well-intentioned non-platform declarer; B5 attacks a malicious actor self-granting the platform role to bypass the ladder entirely.

matches.clause: Isolated tier's strict egress/ingress lockdown with no break-glass/emergency exception (principles 2/3/4/6)

clause_only.clause: Only a party holding the `platform` role may declare a Namespace `infra` (Principle 12 / 'infra is a declaration, not a selection')
clause_only.why_not: A4 argues the rule causes collateral harm (silent rendering to isolated breaks an honest, non-role engineer's well-intentioned low-risk change with no feedback), whereas B4 argues the rule is a governance gap letting a malicious party self-grant the platform role to escape the priced ladder entirely
